nodes.name: Ni foam pretreatment
nodes.procedure: The Ni foam was cut into uniform size (2 * 2.8 cm²), then put in the ultrasonic cleaning 5 min in deionized water, repeated three times to remove impurity on the surface, and then soaked in advanced prepared 3 M hydrochloric acid ultrasonic cleaning for 10 min to remove oxide species, then transferred to deionized water and anhydrous ethanol mixed solution (deionized water (DI): anhydrous ethanol =1:1), carried out in ultrasonic cleaning for 5 min, repeated three times, finally dried at 60°C stay 20 h for later use.
nodes.source_text: Firstly, the Ni foam was cut into uniform size (2 * 2.8 cm²)... finally dried at 60°C stay 20 h for later use.

nodes.name: Hydrothermal synthesis NiCo/NF
nodes.procedure: 3mmol Ni(NO3)2•6H2O + 1mmol Co(NO3)2•6H2O + 1.5mmol CO(NH2)2 and 1.5mM NH4F were dissolved in a beaker with 60 mL DI. Rapidly kept stirring for 30 min until the mixed solution was utterly transparent. We poured the mixture into a hydrothermal reactor, placed the treated Ni foam vertically, and sealed it completely. The system was kept at 120°C for 5 h, and cooled down. Then, the samples were removed with forceps, washed, and dried for 12 h. Ultimately, the final sample markings obtained were named NiCo/NF.

nodes.name: Nitridation to NiCoN/NF
nodes.procedure: We placed the prepared NiCo/NF precursor samples in a tube furnace. And an appropriate amount of urea as a N source was placed upstream of the tube furnace and calcined directly at 400°C for 2 h in nitrogen protection and then cooled to 30°C. The final product obtained was denoted as NiCoN/NF.
nodes.source_text: We placed the prepared NiCo/NF... The final product obtained was denoted as NiCoN/NF.

nodes.name: Phosphorylation to NiCoP/NF
nodes.procedure: The urea was replaced with potassium dihydrogen phosphate and the temperature 400°C was replaced with 350°C and the rest of the steps are the same as above. The end product was named as: NiCoP/NF.
nodes.source_text: The urea was replaced with potassium dihydrogen phosphate... The end product was named as: NiCoP/NF.

nodes.name: Phosphating and nitriding to N-NiCoP/NF
nodes.procedure: The prepared NiCo/NF sample was placed in a tubular furnace, then after a step of phosphating and nitriding treatment to obtain the target product of N-NiCoP/NF.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images show homogeneous lamellar morphology of nanoneedles scattered on uniform nanosheets for N-NiCoP/NF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The SEM, TEM images and XRD patterns of the prepared different samples of NiCo, NiCoN, NiCoP and N-NiCoP are shown in Fig. 2 and S5-10.

properties.features: dense network of nanofibers, high aspect ratio, porous morphology

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns show characteristic peaks of hexagonal NiCoP at 40.9°, 44.9°, 47.6° for both NiCoP and N-NiCoP; N-NiCoP peaks shift to higher angles indicating lattice contraction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The diffraction peaks locate at 47.6°, 44.9° and 40.9°, respectively, belong to planes (210), (201) and (111) of hexagonal NiCoP (PDF#71-2336).

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM shows nanoneedles morphology; N-NiCoP nanoneedles become rougher after N introduction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Meanwhile, the SEM and TEM images (Fig. 2a, 2c and S9) indicate that the smooth NiCoP nanoneedles become rougher after introducing the N element.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows decreased d-spacing of (200) facet from 0.249 nm in NiCoP to 0.243 nm in N-NiCoP; SAED confirms single-crystal phase.
nodes.evidence_snippet: HRTEM images in Fig. 2e and g exhibit that the introduction of trace N leads to the decreased d-spacing of the (200) facet, which is manifested in the reduction of inter-planar spacing from 0.249 nm to 0.243 nm

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM-EDS shows atomic ratio Ni:Co:P:N ≈ 1:0.99:0.08 with uniform elemental distribution in N-NiCoP.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The HRTEM-EDS images of N-NiCoP shows that the atomic ratio was approximately NiCo: P: N = 1:0.99:0.08 (Fig. S11), and traces of N elements are detected

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows Ni 2p3/2 peaks at 853.3 eV (Niδ+), 856.8 eV (Ni oxide), 862.1 eV (satellite) with 0.2 eV negative shift in N-NiCoP; Co 2p3/2 at 778.7 eV (Coδ+) with 0.4 eV shift; P 2p at 128.8/129.7 eV (M-P), 134.4 eV (PO4^3-) with shifts; N 1s at 399.0 eV (Ni-N), 399.9 eV (Co-N).
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the Ni 2p3/2 region, three prominent peaks are located at 853.3, 856.8 and 862.1 eV... The peak value of N-NiCoP shows a 0.2 eV negative shift compared with NiCoP in Ni 2p region.

nodes.characterization_summary: In-situ UV-vis shows CoOOH (360 nm) forms at lower potential (0.48 V) than NiOOH (460 nm) in N-NiCoP; trace N accelerates MOOH formation compared to NiCoP.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Notably, the peak at 360 nm emerges at an earlier stage than the peak at 460 nm in the N-NiCoP sample. This implies that the sample is more likely to form CoOOH species at lower potentials than NiOOH substances during the OER process.

nodes.characterization_summary: CV at various scan rates (20-100 mV/s) used to calculate double layer capacitance Cdl = 15.29 mF/cm² for N-NiCoP (HER region 0.05-0.15 V) and 7.03 mF/cm² (OER region 0.95-1.05 V), indicating larger ECSA.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the calculated Cdl values of N-NiCoP/NF, NiCoP/NF, NiCoN/NF and NiCo/NF are 15.29, 12.75, 11.57 and 6.61 mF cm⁻², respectively
